Consider the finite region bounded by ${x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}=5$ and $x=\sqrt{3},$ where $x\ge 0,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/97ead66fca615e8f9325d445ca14a8478a276e6dc8d2878a2fd5dbea5d880f7a.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by $y=x^3$ and $x=y,$ where $y \leq 0,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis.
current_example.worked_solution:
Writing our first function in terms of $y,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}y={x}^{3}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt[3]{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(y)=\sqrt[3]{y}$ and $g(y)=y.$

Now, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =y \\ y & ={y}^{3} \\ {y}^{3}-y & =0 \\ y({y}^{2}-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence $y=0$ and $y=\pm 1.$ But, since $y \leq 0,$ the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=-1.$

Let's draw our horizontal arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/1ab4ce88964c1a4ce12fdfb93b77810b675bc18e656060629c3544eea47129b2.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $x=g(y)=y,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $x=f(y)=\sqrt[3]{y}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}({[\sqrt[3]{y}]}^{2}-{[y]}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}(\sqrt[3]{{y}^{2}}-{y}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
